RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Harper Alvarez
Member ID: W950863136
Reference number: POC-0FFFC72471-45570
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-14
Requested service: Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
Treating surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Aetna Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551, described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-14. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." This letter, together with the enclosed records, is intended to supply the clinical documentation responsive to that stated reason and to request that the denial be overturned.

I understand Aetna's medical-necessity criteria for this type of surgery are set out in Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0743, "Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion." I have quoted below, in quotation marks, only the language of that policy as I was able to retrieve it directly from Aetna's published bulletin at https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html. I was not able to confirm the "last reviewed"/"last revised" date on that bulletin as it stood on the date of my surgeon's request, and I am not attributing any date to the policy; I ask that Aetna confirm and apply the version of CPB 0743 that was in effect on the date of the request.

CPB 0743 states that Aetna considers the following medically necessary:

"Cervical laminectomy (and/or an anterior and/or posterior cervical discectomy and fusion) for individuals with herniated discs or other causes of spinal cord or nerve root compression (osteophytic spurring, ligamentous hypertrophy) when all of the following criteria are met ...: All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out, including but not limited to significant pathology at other spinal level(s) on the advanced imaging radiology report that is/are not part of the surgical request resulting in incomplete surgical planning; and Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; and Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy ... (unless there is an indication for waiver of requirements for conservative management); and Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression."

Below I address each element of that criteria against the record submitted with the prior authorization request:

1. Other sources of pain/neurological deficit ruled out; single level implicated
The MRI of the cervical spine dated 2026-07-13 identifies a single-level abnormality — C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression — corresponding to the level requested for surgery. [If the radiology report also addresses or rules out pathology at adjacent levels, please attach that section of the report; the summary provided to me does not quote that portion of the report.]

2. Signs or symptoms of neural compression associated with the level being treated
Mrs./Mr. Alvarez has 18 months of progressive neck pain, unrelieved by rest, together with radicular pain and numbness radiating into the right thumb and index finger — a distribution consistent with C6 nerve root involvement — and associated weakness. Physical examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. This directly corresponds to the C5-C6/right C6 findings on the MRI.

3. Advanced imaging showing stenosis or nerve root/cord compression at the corresponding level
The 2026-07-13 MRI documents "severe" right foraminal narrowing with C6 nerve root compression at C5-C6, which meets the severity grade ("moderate, moderate to severe or severe") specified in the policy language quoted above, at the level corresponding to the clinical and examination findings.

4. Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy
The record documents conservative management well in excess of the 6-week minimum referenced in the policy:
- Supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, over 8 weeks (2026-04-27 through 2026-06-22), with 20 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- NSAID therapy for 6 months without adequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-01 that produced only 2 weeks of partial relief.
Taken together, this documents an 8-week supervised course of directed conservative treatment plus 6 months of medication management and an injection, all without durable relief.

5. Activities of daily living limited by symptoms of neural compression
The clinical summary provided to me for this appeal documents radicular pain, numbness, and weakness in the right hand, but does not itself quote specific language about limitation of activities of daily living. [Please have Dr. Reyes' office supply a supplemental statement or clinic note specifically documenting how the neck/arm pain, numbness, and weakness limit the patient's daily activities (e.g., work duties, driving, sleep, grip/fine-motor tasks), as this appears to be part of what the denial letter characterized as "incomplete" documentation.] I am requesting that Aetna hold this appeal open, or treat this letter as a request for peer-to-peer review, so that this supplemental documentation can be submitted before a final decision is issued.

Additional relevant history: there is no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder documented in the record; BMI is 29; the patient is a non-smoker, so smoking/nicotine-cessation documentation requirements elsewhere in CPB 0743 (which apply to certain other fusion indications, not quoted here because they are not the basis for this request) are not at issue.

Based on the above, the record submitted supports that the criteria quoted from CPB 0743 for cervical discectomy and fusion are met, with the possible exception of an explicit statement regarding limitation of activities of daily living, which we are prepared to supplement promptly. I respectfully request that Aetna either (a) overturn the denial based on the enclosed records, or (b) identify, in writing and with reference to the specific unmet criterion, precisely what additional documentation is required, consistent with the "incomplete documentation" reason given in the denial notice, so that it can be furnished within the applicable appeal timeframe.

This appeal is submitted within the deadline stated in the denial notice — the notice states that an appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice (by 2027-02-10) — and I ask that Aetna acknowledge receipt of this appeal and provide the applicable internal appeal decision timeframe, as well as information about any further right to external review through the Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance if the internal appeal is not resolved in the patient's favor.

Enclosed with this letter:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-27 to 2026-06-22, 20 visits)
- Medication history documenting 6 months of NSAID use
- Record of corticosteroid injection dated 2026-04-01 and outcome
- MRI cervical spine report dated 2026-07-13
- Clinic/exam notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic deficit
- [Supplemental statement from Dr. Reyes addressing functional/ADL limitation, if available]
- A copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-14

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address/phone/email above. I can be reached at [patient phone number] to discuss this appeal or to schedule a peer-to-peer review between Aetna's medical director and Dr. Reyes.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Harper Alvarez
Member ID: W950863136
